id: General Rules|Magical Consumables|Turning Effects into Consumables
title: Turning Effects into Consumables
summary: General guidance for creating Magic Item Consumables from Ancestry Traits, Talents, Features, Equipment Properties, and Magic Item Properties.
text:
This section provides general guidance on how GMs can create their own Magic Item Consumables from effects (such as Ancestry Traits, Talents, Features, Equipment Properties, and Magic Item Properties).

ACTIVATION COST
The AP cost to use a consumable created from an effect should be equal to the effect’s base AP cost (minimum 1).
keywords: magical consumable magic item creation balance activation AP cost ancestry trait talent feature equipment property

title: Spell Consumables
summary: A Consumable created from a Spell uses the Spell’s Duration and derives Magic Power from its base MP, Enhancements, and AP cost.
text:
A Consumable created from a Spell has the following characteristics:

• Duration: Spell’s Duration
• Magic Power: Base MP + Enhancements: MP + (AP / 2)

EXAMPLE: HASTE
The Haste Spell costs 1 AP and 1 MP. A potion that grants the benefit of a Haste Spell should cost 1 AP to drink and it would have 1 Magic Power. If the effect included the Phased Movement Enhancement (1 MP), then it would have 2 Magic Power.

EXAMPLE: FIREBALL
The Fireball Spell costs 2 AP. A bomb that casts Fireball when thrown would require 2 AP to use (such as 1 AP to prime and 1 AP to throw), and it would have 0 Magic Power.
keywords: spell consumable potion bomb duration magic power MP AP enhancement Haste Fireball

title: Ancestry Trait Consumables
summary: An Ancestry Trait Consumable lasts until a Long Rest and derives Magic Power from the Trait’s Ancestry Point cost, Enhancements, and AP cost.
text:
A Consumable created from an Ancestry Trait has the following characteristics:

• Duration: Until Long Rest
• Magic Power: Ancestry Trait Points + Enhancements: MP + (AP / 2)

EXAMPLE: DRACONIC BREATH WEAPON
The Draconic Breath Weapon Ancestry Trait costs 2 Ancestry Points. A potion that grants the benefit of Draconic Breath Weapon until you complete a Long Rest should cost 1 AP to drink and have 2 Magic Power. If the first use of the Breath Weapon had an additional 2 MP worth of damage, then the potion should have 4 Magic Power.
keywords: ancestry trait consumable duration long rest magic power ancestry points MP AP Draconic Breath Weapon

id: General Rules|Magical Consumables|Once per Combat Feature & Talent Consumables
title: Once per Combat Feature & Talent Consumables
summary: A consumable based on a once-per-combat Feature or Talent uses the effect’s Duration and a Magic Power formula that includes MP and SP.
text:
A Consumable created from a Feature or Talent that replenishes uses when you roll Initiative or is designed to be used once per combat has the following characteristics:

• Duration: Effect’s Duration
• Magic Power: 2 + MP + (SP / 2)

EXAMPLE: ARCANE SIGIL
A Wizard’s Arcane Sigil costs 1 AP and 1 MP to activate, and is designed to be used once per combat. A rune that creates a Wizard’s Sigil should cost 1 AP to activate and have 3 Magic Power.
keywords: once per combat feature talent consumable initiative magic power MP SP Arcane Sigil Wizard rune

id: General Rules|Magical Consumables|Continuous Feature & Talent Consumables
title: Continuous Feature & Talent Consumables
summary: A consumable based on a continuously usable Feature or Talent defaults to lasting until a Long Rest and adds 5 to its MP- and SP-based Magic Power.
text:
A Consumable created from a Feature or Talent that can be used continuously throughout the day has the following characteristics:

• Duration: Effect’s Duration (Until Long Rest if not stated)
• Magic Power: 5 + MP + (SP / 2)

EXAMPLE: FAVORED TERRAIN
A Ranger’s Favored Terrain Feature has no cost to activate. A scroll that grants the benefits of 2 Favored Terrains until you complete a Long Rest should have 5 Magic Power.

DC TIP
Be mindful when turning a Talent or Feature into a magic item that it can make characters who’ve taken those Talents or Features feel less special.
keywords: continuous feature talent consumable duration long rest magic power MP SP Favored Terrain Ranger scroll DC tip

title: Equipment Property Consumables
summary: An Equipment Property Consumable lasts until a Long Rest and has twice the Property’s Equipment Property Point cost in Magic Power.
text:
A Consumable created from an Equipment Property (Weapon, Spell Focus, Armor, or Shield) has the following characteristics:

• Duration: Until Long Rest
• Magic Power: 2 x Equipment Property Points

EXAMPLE: POWERFUL
Powerful costs 2 Spell Focus Property Points. An infusion oil that grants the befits of the Powerful Spell Focus Property should have 4 Magic Power.

DC TIP
Applying an Equipment Property to a different type of equipment does not change what type of equipment it is. For example, if you apply a Spell Focus Property to a Shield, holding the Shield does not count as performing Somatic Components for casting a Spell.
keywords: equipment property consumable weapon spell focus armor shield duration long rest magic power property points Powerful infusion oil somatic components

id: General Rules|Magical Consumables|Magic Item Property Consumables
title: Magic Item Property Consumables
summary: A Magic Item Property Consumable lasts until a Long Rest and uses the Property’s own Magic Power value.
text:
A Consumable created from a Magic Item Property has the following characteristics:

• Duration: Until Long Rest
• Magic Power: Magic Item Property Magic Power

EXAMPLE: TRUESIGHT
The Truesight Magic Item Property has 6 Magic Power. An eyedrop that grants Truesight until you complete a Long Rest should have 6 Magic Power.
keywords: magic item property consumable duration long rest magic power Truesight eyedrop
